title: A Note on Distance-Fall Colorings: the distance-2 fall 3-colouring theorem (Theorem 2.1)
author: Wayne Goddard and Sonwabile Mafunda
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the note's headline result and its short proof is a minimal-counterexample argument that is not available from any standard textbook. Even with the note's own definitions of a fall colouring, of a distance-2 fall colouring, of a dominating and independent distance-2 dominating set and of a 2-good and a 2-bad vertex supplied as context, the proof still has to choose the right potential function (the number of 2-bad vertices over all proper 3-colourings of G) and then run two recolouring cases: first, if a 2-bad vertex v has a neighbour w1 of degree one, recolour w1 with the colour missing from N[v] and check that the colouring stays proper and that the count of 2-bad vertices strictly drops; second, if every neighbour of v has degree at least two, derive from the 2-badness of v that N(v) is monochromatic and that v and all vertices of its second neighbourhood share a colour, then recolour v itself with the colour missing from N[v] and verify that v becomes 2-good, that every neighbour of v stays 2-good and that no previously 2-good vertex becomes 2-bad. Both cases contradict the minimality of the chosen colouring, which is the whole content of the theorem. A qualifying examination in graph theory asks for fall-colouring constructions and for domination bounds, not for this minimality-and-recolouring transfer, which is a research contribution of the note; at the same time the argument needs no external theory, which places it in the upper half of the qualifying-to-research range rather than beyond ordinary research practice: H2.
